title: Stop Manlet Hate (A Message to Short Men)
summary: A long talk to short men about how society, women and other men treat them, drawing on NH's own experience of being short until a growth spurt at 15. He gives his height chart, explains why short lifters dominate fitness media and why their advice can hurt tall lifters, and argues heightism is real. He ends by telling short men to reject fake positivity and victimhood, accept their height and build strength and self-respect.
claims: His height chart: under 5'0" is dwarfism, 5'0"-5'3" a severe manlet, 5'4"-5'6" a manlet, 5'7"-5'9" average, 5'10"-6'0" above average, over 6'0" clearly not a manlet
Many fitness influencers are around 5'6"; shorter men are over-represented because they look big on camera, which the audience takes as competence
Short men look jacked faster because they have less frame to fill: a 5'6" man can look great at 160-170 lb within about two years, while a 6'2" man needs at least 200 lb and many more years
Online there is no scale, so short lifters close to the camera look huge; his 'juiced or manlet' game finds the answer is manlet about 90% of the time
Advice from short lifters can injure tall ones: ass-to-grass squats make a tall lifter's lumbar spine flex, and conventional deadlifts round a tall lifter's back
The 'no isolation, just spam chin-ups and bench' advice mostly comes from short lifters for whom it works; it doesn't transfer to taller people
Every fitness YouTuber speaks from their own perspective; at 6 ft he needs about 200 lb to be big, so calling 160 lb small is his frame talking
Short lifters can get results faster but have lower potential for absolute strength and absolute size
He cites a campus experiment where most men overstated their height when measured; only men about 5'11" and taller didn't lie
He was short until 15 (about 5'2" from age 10 to 15), was disrespected daily, then grew almost a foot in 2-3 years and was suddenly treated with respect
A boy who bullied him in middle school greeted him warmly and wanted to be friends after his growth spurt
Respect between men outside intimate relationships is largely based on perceived threat (the chihuahua vs pit bull effect)
Mocking short men remains socially acceptable while mocking many other groups is taboo
His wife, asked off-guard, admitted she wouldn't have dated him if he were three inches shorter
Women have height requirements, not preferences; even short women often require men around 6 ft, shrinking the dating pool of short men by millions per inch
The 'big five' of male attractiveness to women are face, money, status, fame and height; height is the most immediately visible, and personality matters later to cement the relationship
He believes it is better to be ugly and tall than short and handsome
Men are tools and women are works of art: a tool can be ugly as long as it is useful
Short men who lift or get rich to compensate get mocked for 'Napoleon syndrome', so they are damned either way
He cites short men as about twice as likely to take their own lives as taller men and eight times as likely as women
Victimhood is a choice; short men's luck is that the victim label is slapped on them harshly rather than offered kindly, so they can reject it
Reject fake positivity like 'short king'; become a king instead of calling yourself one
Accept what you are rather than denying it; you can't change your height but you can change your relationship with it and turn the weakness into armour
Emancipation only comes through strength: make yourself strong enough that the oppression stops mattering
What makes a man is what's inside, not the distance from toes to scalp
He was on the verge of becoming bitter toward women and everyone before his growth spurt saved him
When people mock you for lifting or improving, it proves your self-improvement bothers them and you should keep going
